sentences.text: Klamelisaurus measured approximately 13 meters in length, with its neck comprising half of that total distance.
The preserved neck vertebrae number nine, though estimates suggest the full count reached sixteen, extending the neck to about 6.5 meters.
A distinctive trait identified by researchers includes irregular, plate-like extensions located on the spinoprezygapophyseal laminae of the neck bones.
Deep openings were also discovered on the sides of these vertebrae, situated below the spinoprezygapophyseal laminae and ahead of the spinodiapophyseal fossae.
The forelimb was roughly three-quarters the length of the hindlimb, with the ulna and tibia measuring two-thirds the length of the humerus and femur respectively.
The type species Klamelisaurus gobiensis was named by Zhao Xijin in 1993 based on a partial skeleton found in 1982 near the abandoned town of Jiangjunmiao.
This skeleton was unearthed 35 km north of Jiangjunmiao within the eastern Junggar Basin.
Work to prepare and restore the specimen began in 1985 after it was transported to Beijing.
The species Klamelisaurus gobiensis was formally described by Zhao Xijin in 1993.
The fossils were located in the Gobi Desert, specifically within the Shishugou Formation in Xinjiang, China.
The holotype, cataloged as IVPP V9492, was found in a Shishugou Formation layer dating to the Oxfordian, approximately 160 million years ago.
The holotype consists of a partial skeleton that lacks a skull.
The postcranial skeleton is fairly complete, missing only the front of the neck, the left shoulder girdle, the left forelimb, and the feet.
Klamelisaurus was a herbivorous sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Middle Jurassic in the Shishugou Formation of China.
It is classified as a medium-sized sauropod.
Gregory S. Paul estimated the length at 13 meters and weight at 6 tons in 2016, based on the hypothesis that the specimen represented an adult form.
Zhao originally classified Klamelisaurus as the sole member of the new subfamily Klamelisaurinae within the order Bothrosauropodoidea.
In 1993, Zhao classified Klamelisaurus as the sole genus in the new subfamily Klamelisaurinae.
In 1993, Zhao erected a new subfamily, Klamelisaurinae, of which Klamelisaurus was the only member.
Phylogenetic analyses suggest Klamelisaurus belongs to the family Mamenchisauridae, a group of primarily Chinese sauropods.
Moore and colleagues termed the group containing Klamelisaurus and related sauropods the "core Mamenchisaurus-like taxa".
The parent group of Klamelisaurus is Mamenchisauridae.
Researchers highlighted the need for further redescriptions and revisions of sauropods like Mamenchisaurus and Omeisaurus to resolve classification debates.
It lived during the middle Jurassic, approximately 165 to 161 million years ago in the Oxfordian, in what is now Asia.
The time range is the Callovian, from 165.3 to 161.5 million years ago.
Paul suggested in 2010 and 2016 that Klamelisaurus might be the adult form of Bellusaurus.
In 2018, Moore and colleagues refuted the hypothesis that Klamelisaurus is the adult form of Bellusaurus.
The hypothesis that Bellusaurus is a juvenile Klamelisaurus has been rejected due to anatomical differences and geological age differences.
Moore and colleagues noted that Klamelisaurus and Bellusaurus were not contemporaries, as the Klamelisaurus holotype comes from older rock layers.
Moore and colleagues identified differences in vertebral pneumatic features between Klamelisaurus and Bellusaurus that cannot be explained by age differences.
Bellusaurus possessed specific pneumatic features in dorsal neural spines and arches that Klamelisaurus lacked, contradicting expected patterns for euhelopodids and mamenchisaurids.
Moore and colleagues noted that bifurcated neural spines and wing-shaped processes on rear dorsals might vary with age, complicating the distinction between Klamelisaurus and Bellusaurus.
Moore and colleagues refuted the possible synonymy of Klamelisaurus and Bellusaurus in 2018, noting that the differences between the genera were slightly older and not ontogenetic.
